## A multi-level agent orchestration demo {.section-title}

::: {.slide-subtitle}
Building a transparent and traceable system with multi-level agents
:::

::: {.slide-deckline}
Using the Agents SDK to execute multi-agent research like a highly-governed analytical pipeline for auditability.
:::

::: {.three-col .top-gap}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Control plane</div>

Python owns workflow state, concurrency, budgets, retries, validation, and release policy.
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Inference plane</div>

The OpenAI Agents SDK gives each role a bounded model loop, tools, typed output, and hosted traces.
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Evidence plane</div>

Source records, claims, artifacts, audit history, and eval results remain inspectable after the run.
:::
:::

## A familiar modeling metaphor

::: {.two-col .wide-left}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    Q["Policy question"] --> X["Feature construction<br/>research plan"]
    X --> E1["Expert model<br/>government"]
    X --> E2["Expert model<br/>legal"]
    X --> E3["Expert model<br/>academic"]
    E1 --> M["Meta-estimator<br/>manager synthesis"]
    E2 --> M
    E3 --> M
    M --> D["Draft report"]
    D --> V["Diagnostics +<br/>constrained re-work"]
    V --> O["Released output<br/>plus audit trail"]
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Mixture of experts</div>

Branches specialize by evidence domain. Managers reconcile authority, disagreement, and uncertainty.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">No silent imputation</div>

A failed branch becomes explicit missingness with a typed status and limitation. It does not disappear.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Diagnostics before release</div>

Validation and adversarial review inspect the report after generation, when defects can be localized.
:::
:::
:::

## Who controls what?

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Python workflow</div>

- Selects branches and managers
- Starts concurrent tasks
- Enforces retries and time limits
- Carries run state and source IDs
- Applies deterministic validators
- Decides whether content is released or withheld
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Agents SDK runtime</div>

- Executes the agent turn loop
- Calls hosted and local tools
- Validates structured model output
- Returns raw responses and usage
- Emits hosted trace spans and metadata
- Supports agents exposed as tools
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
The app keeps policy and reliability decisions in ordinary code. The SDK handles bounded agent execution.
:::

::: {.notes}

## The agent topology is an explicit model graph

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph SP["Specialist layer"]
      G["Government sources"]
      L["Legal and regulatory"]
      T["Think tank and academic"]
      C["Consumer and industry"]
      A["Advocacy and equity"]
      X["Global comparison"]
    end
    subgraph MG["Manager layer"]
      PM["Policy manager"]
      IM["Industry manager"]
      AM["Advocacy manager"]
      GM["Global manager"]
    end
    G --> PM
    L --> PM
    T --> PM
    C --> IM
    A --> AM
    X --> GM
    PM --> WR["Synthesis writer"]
    IM --> WR
    AM --> WR
    GM --> WR
    WR --> RV["Reviewer and re-work"]
```

::: {.caption-bar}
A handoff is the structured package passed from one agent to the next. An edge is the arrow that shows this transfer. Every package follows a defined format, and every agent has a named role, scope, source preference, and response rule.
:::

```python
    name="Government Sources Researcher",
    instructions=role_and_scope,
    model=config.openai_model,
    tools=[WebSearchTool(...)],
    output_type=agent_output_schema(
        SpecialistFinding

)
```

The schema turns prose generation into a measurable interface: claims, sources, confidence, uncertainty, limitations, and branch status.

## A bounded SDK call, with tools and trace metadata

::: {.two-col .code-slide}
::: {.panel}
```python
agent = build_specialist_agent(
    branch=assignment.branch.value,
    config=context.config,
    tools=backend.agent_tools(),
)

result = await Runner.run(
    agent,
    input=payload,
    max_turns=config.max_turns_per_agent,
    run_config=RunConfig(
        workflow_name="housing-policy-research",
        trace_id=context.trace_id,
        trace_metadata={
            "run_id": context.run_id,
            "branch": assignment.branch.value,
        },
    ),
)
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>1</b><span>Build the role from versioned instructions and a Pydantic output type.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>2</b><span>Attach the hosted <code>WebSearchTool</code> only in live mode.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>3</b><span>Bound the run with <code>max_turns</code> and workflow policy.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>4</b><span>Group SDK spans with app run and branch metadata.</span>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/specialists.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/tools/research.py`

## Allows for concurrent processing without losing track of workers

::: {.two-col .wide-left}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Workflow
    participant S as Semaphore
    participant A as Specialist A
    participant B as Specialist B
    participant C as Specialist C
    W->>S: gather assignments
    S->>A: acquire slot
    S->>B: acquire slot
    S->>C: wait
    A-->>W: COMPLETED finding
    B--xW: parse or tool failure
    W->>B: bounded retry
    B-->>W: FAILED finding + limitation
    S->>C: acquire released slot
    C-->>W: COMPLETED finding
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Controlled parallel work</div>

Only a set number of specialists run at once. When one finishes, the next waiting branch starts.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Recorded failure</div>

If a branch still fails after retry, the workflow records the reason so managers can account for the missing research.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Incomplete beats invented</div>

If the evidence is too thin, the manager reports incomplete coverage instead of filling gaps with invented claims.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/workflows/research_workflow.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/specialists.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/managers.py`
:::

## The initial plan is deterministic in this implementation (example con't)

::: {.two-col .wide-left}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Q["User question"] --> G["Guardrail check"]
    G --> B["build_brief()"]
    B --> P["build_plan()"]
    P --> A["10 typed<br/>assignments"]
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-blue}
<div class="panel-title">What the brief adds</div>

U.S. jurisdiction, sophisticated policy audience, balanced stakeholders, and a current plus 5-to-10-year horizon.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">What the plan adds</div>

Branch objective, manager destination, scope boundaries, preferred sources, required questions, and typed handoff rules.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.persona-strip}
<b>Planner behavior</b> Python applies fixed routing rules. This keeps the same question on the same research path, makes branch selection easy to test, and avoids spending a model call on a decision the application can define directly.
:::

::: {.notes}

## The ten specialist personas turn one question into distinct research perspectives (example con't)

::: {.specialist-intro}
<b>Shared specialist persona:</b> careful, curious, skeptical evidence researcher. State what evidence establishes, suggests, and cannot answer; never act as advocate, lawyer, or general explainer.
:::

::: {.portfolio-grid}
::: {.portfolio-column .accent-top}
<div class="portfolio-title">Policy portfolio</div>
<p><b>Government sources</b><br><span>Official baseline, public authority, administrative evidence</span></p>
<p><b>Legal and regulatory</b><br><span>Controlling law, agency interpretation, unresolved legal questions</span></p>
<p><b>Think tank and academic</b><br><span>Methods, mechanisms, magnitude, contrary empirical evidence</span></p>
:::

::: {.portfolio-column}
<div class="portfolio-title">Industry portfolio</div>
<p><b>Consumer</b><br><span>Access, affordability, terms, default, borrower welfare</span></p>
<p><b>Loan originator</b><br><span>Underwriting operations, incentives, cost, feasibility</span></p>
<p><b>Servicing</b><br><span>Transfers, disputes, loss mitigation, post-close operations</span></p>
<p><b>Secondary market</b><br><span>Pricing, liquidity, capital, credit-risk transfer</span></p>
:::

::: {.portfolio-column}
<div class="portfolio-title">Advocacy portfolio</div>
<p><b>Consumer advocacy</b><br><span>Transparency, contestability, fees, remedies</span></p>
<p><b>Disadvantaged communities</b><br><span>Distribution by geography, income, race, tenure, rurality</span></p>
<p><b>Financial sustainability</b><br><span>Stress, adverse selection, moral hazard, public exposure</span></p>
:::
:::

## Example agent persona for 'Government Sources Research' (example con't)

::: {.two-col .wide-right}
::: {.persona-card}
<div class="persona-label">AGENT PERSONA</div>
<div class="persona-name">Government Sources Researcher</div>

Skeptical public-sector evidence researcher. Prefer statutes, regulations, agency documents, official evaluations, and administrative data. Separate current policy from proposals and inference.

<div class="persona-rule">Out of scope: general industry commentary unless an official record summarizes it.</div>
:::

::: {.handoff-contract}
<div class="contract-row"><b>Objective</b><span>Establish current policy, authority, implementation requirements, public evidence, and unresolved issues.</span></div>
<div class="contract-row"><b>Context</b><span>One branch of a larger workflow; a manager will compare it with legal and academic siblings.</span></div>
<div class="contract-row"><b>Scope</b><span>Official baseline, policy history, government analysis, documented effects.</span></div>
<div class="contract-row"><b>Questions</b><span>What is established? What is contested? What should siblings or implementers answer?</span></div>
<div class="contract-row"><b>Source rule</b><span>Use stable source IDs; complete URLs stay only in source records.</span></div>
<div class="contract-row"><b>Output rule</b><span>Return only the typed finding object, with no preamble or Markdown fence.</span></div>
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
The sub-agent receives enough downstream context to be useful, but no authority to expand the question or write the final report.
:::

## Three manager agents reconcile provided evidence (example con't)

::: {.manager-grid}
::: {.manager-column .accent-top}
<div class="persona-label">POLICY RESEARCH MANAGER</div>
<div class="manager-persona">Calm, skeptical policy integrator. Reconcile authority, baseline, empirical mechanisms, and uncertainty.</div>
<div class="manager-input">3 branches → 9 reconciled claims</div>
<p><b>Preserved uncertainty:</b> no direct study resolves whether an AVM-plus workflow satisfies consumer-specific verification.</p>
:::

::: {.manager-column}
<div class="persona-label">INDUSTRY RESEARCH MANAGER</div>
<div class="manager-persona">Operations-minded market integrator. Compare consumer, origination, servicing, and risk-transfer evidence.</div>
<div class="manager-input">4 branches → 10 reconciled claims</div>
<p><b>Preserved uncertainty:</b> no direct estimate of approval, default, servicing, CRT, or taxpayer effects.</p>
:::

::: {.manager-column}
<div class="persona-label">ADVOCACY RESEARCH MANAGER</div>
<div class="manager-persona">Equity-conscious, evidence-disciplined integrator. Identify who benefits, who bears risk, and where evidence is thin.</div>
<div class="manager-input">3 branches → 8 reconciled claims</div>
<p><b>Preserved uncertainty:</b> aggregate paperwork reduction does not establish equitable benefit.</p>
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
All three managers agreed on a bounded use case and the absence of direct outcome evidence, while retaining different legal, operational, and distributional concerns.
:::

## The writer composes from the manager packages (example con't)

::: {.two-col}
::: {.persona-card}
<div class="persona-label">AGENT PERSONA</div>
<div class="persona-name">Synthesis Writer</div>

Lucid, disciplined policy writer. Turn reconciled evidence into a decision-ready report without smoothing away disagreement or uncertainty. Never generate new facts or act as lobbyist or legal adviser.

<div class="persona-rule">Input contract: 3 manager syntheses, 55 source IDs, the policy brief, handoff context, and quality requirements.</div>
:::

::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">What the first draft produced</div>

- 6 report sections plus executive summary and decision matrix
- Explicit evidence gaps and limitations
- A recommendation against nationwide AVM-only replacement
- A conditional, reversible evaluation only after legal clearance

<div class="finding-bottom"><b>Key distinction:</b> estimated market rent is a forecast; borrower-specific records seek to establish actual or supportable cash flow.</div>
:::

## The reviewer flags defects for revision (example con't)

::: {.review-loop}
::: {.persona-card .reviewer-card}
<div class="persona-label">ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER PERSONA</div>
<div class="persona-name">Exacting, constructive challenger</div>
Inspect grounding, citations, legal calibration, causal claims, missing counterarguments, and security. Identify corrections; do not silently rewrite the report.
:::

<div class="review-arrow">7 findings →</div>

::: {.revision-example}
<div class="example-label">HIGH-SEVERITY FINDING F1</div>
<p><b>Flag:</b> existing GSE market-rent workflows could be read as authorizing an AVM-based method.</p>
<p><b>Required correction:</b> state that current precedent is limited to appraisal-supported workflows and that AVM use needs independent legal and program approval.</p>
:::
:::

::: {.persona-strip}
<b>Revision-writer persona</b> Same disciplined synthesis writer, now constrained by the review package: revise only material issues, retain valid citations, and invent no evidence.
:::

::: {.score-row}
<span><b>0.84</b><strong>Grounding</strong><small>claims supported</small></span><span><b>0.93</b><strong>Balance</strong><small>competing views represented</small></span><span><b>0.88</b><strong>Calibration</strong><small>confidence matches evidence</small></span><span><b>1.00</b><strong>Security</strong><small>untrusted instructions resisted</small></span><span><b>1</b><strong>Revision</strong><small>revision round</small></span>
:::

## How are metadata organized into a source ledger

::: {.four-grid}
::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">01 | Acquire</div>

Specialists retrieve official, legal, academic, industry, advocacy, or comparative evidence.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">02 | Normalize</div>

Every source becomes a `SourceRecord` with a short stable ID, URL, publisher, date, and source tier.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">03 | Join</div>

Claims refer to source IDs. URLs stay in the source record, which keeps citations resolvable and deduplicated.
:::

::: {.panel .mini .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">04 | Validate</div>

The workflow rejects missing references, malformed comparisons, and unsupported report claims.
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
Think of the ledger as data lineage for qualitative evidence: every released claim must have a reproducible path back to a source record.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/tools/source_store.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/models/domain.py`
- `docs/architecture.md`
:::

## Validation and re-work are transparent in run and end product

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    D["Draft report"] --> V["Deterministic validation"]
    V --> R["Withhold + re-work<br/>flagged targets"]
    R --> C{"Defect cleared?"}
    C -- "yes" --> P["Replace target"]
    C -- "no" --> W["Keep withheld"]
    P --> A["Audit report"]
    W --> A
```
:::

::: {.stack .validation-stack}
::: {.callout-blue}
<div class="panel-title">Constrained repair</div>

The re-work agent can change only flagged targets. It cannot silently rewrite healthy sections.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Auditable diff</div>

The audit records what failed, what was withheld, the attempted revision, and the final disposition.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Fail closed by section</div>

Unresolved unsupported content remains withheld while valid report sections can still be released.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Periodic check</div>

System diagnostics could periodically summarize recent revision trends and identify instructions that may need updating.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/rework.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/prompts/rework.md`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/tools/source_store.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/workflows/research_workflow.py`
:::

## Mitigating hallucinations using adversarial review

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Primary model</div>

The writer synthesizes manager outputs into a decision-oriented report with claims, caveats, alternatives, and source references.
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Challenger model</div>

The reviewer looks for overclaiming, omitted counterevidence, authority mismatches, weak country analogies, and unsupported recommendations.
:::
:::

::: {.flow-row}
<span>Draft</span><i></i><span>Review findings</span><i></i><span>One bounded revision</span><i></i><span>Final validation</span>
:::

::: {.principle}
Separation of roles matters: generation optimizes coherence; challenge optimizes defect discovery.
:::

## Keeping track of cost and efficiency

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">What is measured</div>

- Requests per interaction
- Input, cached input, output, and reasoning tokens
- Wall-clock duration per agent and stage
- Completed or failed status
- Model and pricing version
:::

::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">What is estimated</div>

<div class="cost-formula">C<sub>est</sub> = (t<sub>in</sub>r<sub>in</sub> + t<sub>cache</sub>r<sub>cache</sub> + t<sub>out</sub>r<sub>out</sub>) / 10<sup>6</sup></div>

<div class="cost-terms"><span><b>t</b> = token count</span><span><b>r</b> = published rate per million tokens</span><span><b>in / cache / out</b> = uncached input, cached input, and output</span></div>

The equation multiplies recorded token usage by published rates. This is an estimate based on published costs, not actually exposing platform.openai.com billing data.
:::
:::

::: {.warning-strip}
<b>Why doesn't the app have real pricing from the API calls?</b> <b>Short answer:</b> A response returns token usage, not the final account-level dollar charge. Reconciled spend belongs in OpenAI's organization Costs API or billing dashboard, so the app uses a versioned pricing table and labels the result as an estimate.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/telemetry/usage.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/telemetry/pricing.py`
- `docs/model-pricing.md`
- OpenAI API pricing: https://platform.openai.com/pricing
- OpenAI organization usage and costs: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/admin/subresources/organization/subresources/usage
:::

## How is Promptfoo used vs. regular runs?

::: {.eval-lanes}
::: {.eval-lane .accent-top}
<div class="lane-label">Normal research run</div>

<div class="lane-flow"><span>User question</span><i></i><span>Application workflow</span><i></i><span>Artifacts</span></div>

The CLI starts the agents and writes the report, audit trail, telemetry, and usage report. <b>Promptfoo is not called.</b>
:::

::: {.eval-lane}
<div class="lane-label">Evaluation run</div>

<div class="lane-flow"><span>Promptfoo</span><i></i><span>Python provider</span><i></i><span>Workflow output</span><i></i><span>Assertions</span></div>

Promptfoo repeatedly invokes configured variants, scores their structured outputs, and shows which test cells passed or failed.
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
Promptfoo compares and regression-tests the architecture. Python and the Agents SDK orchestrate production research.
:::

## Four specific terms used in Promptfoo structure

::: {.four-grid .term-grid}
::: {.panel .mini .accent-top}
<div class="term-number">01</div>
<div class="panel-title">Prompt</div>

The task template kept the same across tests. <b>Example:</b> send the same research-request wording to every provider.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="term-number">02</div>
<div class="panel-title">Provider</div>

An adapter that runs one candidate system. <b>Example:</b> compare the full agent hierarchy with a shallow baseline.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="term-number">03</div>
<div class="panel-title">Test case</div>

One scenario plus its input values. <b>Example:</b> run a mortgage-portability question or a prompt-injection case.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="term-number">04</div>
<div class="panel-title">Assertion</div>

A rule that scores the result. <b>Example:</b> verify every cited source ID exists in the source ledger.
:::
:::

::: {.equation-strip}
<b>One evaluation cell</b> = one prompt x one provider x one test case, checked by one or more assertions
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `evals/promptfooconfig.yaml`
- `evals/datasets/offline.yaml`
- `evals/assertions/quality.py`
- Promptfoo assertions: https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/
:::

## Promptfoo is configured for 52 comparable test cells using offline evaluation

## As example, the Python provider is an adapter around ResearchWorkflow

::: {.two-col .code-slide}
::: {.panel}
```python
def call_api(prompt, options, context):
    config = AppConfig(
        research_provider="offline",
        enable_manager_reconciliation=True,
        enable_adversarial_review=True,
    )
    request = UserResearchRequest(
        question=context["vars"]["question"],
        mode=RunMode.FAST,
        accept_defaults=True,
    )
    package = asyncio.run(
        ResearchWorkflow(config).run(request)
    )
    return {"output": package.model_dump_json()}
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>1</b><span>Promptfoo passes one test case to a normal Python function.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>2</b><span>The provider builds the same workflow class used by the CLI, configured for fixtures.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>3</b><span>The workflow returns the complete typed research package as JSON.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>4</b><span>Promptfoo sends that JSON to the configured assertion functions.</span>
:::
:::
:::

## An ablation removes one mechanism to test whether it matters

::: {.ablation-definition}
<div class="definition-word">Ablation</div>
<div class="definition-text">A controlled experiment that removes one component while holding the dataset and scoring rules constant.</div>
:::

::: {.ablation-grid}
::: {.ablation-card .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Full system</div>

Reference result with every configured mechanism enabled.
:::
::: {.ablation-card}
<div class="panel-title">No legal branch</div>

Does legal research improve validity and issue spotting?
:::
::: {.ablation-card}
<div class="panel-title">No manager reconciliation</div>

Does manager synthesis reduce contradictions and improve integration?
:::
::: {.ablation-card}
<div class="panel-title">No adversarial review</div>

Does challenge-and-revision improve defect recall and calibration?
:::
::: {.ablation-card}
<div class="panel-title">Shallow baseline</div>

Does the full hierarchy earn its added latency and complexity?
:::
:::

::: {.equation-strip}
The current matrix runs <b>26 cases x 8 variants = 208 cells</b>, including additional “no global,” “no advocacy,” and “no clarification” variants.
:::

## What Promptfoo's implementation here is checking

::: {.two-col .boundary-grid}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="boundary-label implemented">Implemented now</div>

- Output schema validates
- Required report sections exist
- Referenced source IDs resolve
- Citation coverage clears the current rule
- Review output is present when required
- Dedicated cases exercise injection resistance
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="boundary-label future">Not currently wired into Promptfoo</div>

- SDK trajectory assertions: verify which agents, tools, and handoffs ran, and in what order
- OTLP span assertions: inspect exported OpenTelemetry records for timing, tool calls, and errors
- Accurate application token and cost reporting
- Every metric listed in `thresholds.yaml`
- Human grading of policy rigor or factual sufficiency
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
Promptfoo catches repeatable structural regressions. The application’s own artifacts and usage report remain the source for detailed traces, agent interactions, tokens, time, and estimated cost.
:::
